<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-adamw4bit-715c8ec7" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0b06e014d4785862">Why does state quantization affect later steps?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadamw4bit">Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley / Nubank</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>First and second moments recur, so stored errors enter optimization after decoding at the next step. Control their effects on preconditioning and future updates, not merely bytes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Repeated downward rounding of v can inflate effective learning rates across steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12444">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12444-adamw4bit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0b06e014d4785862">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:adamw4bit" data-paper-title="Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c8a13b370455cc00">Why control second-moment rounding in preconditioner space in 4-bit AdamW?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadamw4bit">Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley / Nubank</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bias correction, square root, and reciprocal nonlinearly transform moment error into update error. ZIP-SR uses preconditioner values for stochastic rounding; ZE-EDEN handles code points and scales. Error persists through state recurrence. Use working moments for the update before packing.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small moment differences can greatly change reciprocal-root steps, so raw moment MSE misses the effective gradient scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12444">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12444-adamw4bit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c8a13b370455cc00">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:adamw4bit" data-paper-title="Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a2ee36b4cc02d185">How do ZIP-SR and ZE-EDEN store second moments differently?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadamw4bit">Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley / Nubank</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ZIP-SR stochastically rounds in preconditioner space. ZE-EDEN excludes zero code points and calibrates block scales. Compare training loss and actual persistent bytes, not a generic four-bit rounding table.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Randomly choosing adjacent codes differs from rescaling blocks to avoid zero codes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12444">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12444-adamw4bit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a2ee36b4cc02d185">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:adamw4bit" data-paper-title="Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8b106936b90fd09d">Should current working moments be quantized before updating parameters?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aadamw4bit">Rounding in Preconditioner Space: Redesigning 4-bit AdamW Optimizer-State Quantization</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Berkeley / Nubank</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Decode old state, form new working moments, update using their unquantized values, then pack for persistence. Reversing the order injects error into the current step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use v to precondition this step before compressing it for the next.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12444">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.12444-adamw4bit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8b106936b90fd09d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:af-muon" data-paper-title="AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-af-muon-b7027d08" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-31b949c759ccfa99">Why use different updates for different parameter types?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaf-muon">AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hidden matrices, tied vocabulary, and one-dimensional parameters have different geometry and support. Use Muon, support-aware capped vocabulary directions, and RMS respectively.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sparsely visited input embedding row differs from a dense hidden matrix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01395">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01395-af-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-31b949c759ccfa99">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:af-muon" data-paper-title="AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-bc1646d03073e9ba">Why not apply ordinary Muon to tied embeddings?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaf-muon">AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tied vocab weights support sparse input lookup and dense output classification with different gradient geometry. AF-Muon uses spectral updates for hidden matrices, support-aware capped directions for vocab, and RMS for vectors. Output gradients can touch rows absent from the input.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An unseen input word can still receive classification gradient as an output candidate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01395">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01395-af-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bc1646d03073e9ba">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:af-muon" data-paper-title="AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-91844685fea05438">How does support-aware capped direction differ from unit-normalizing every vocab row?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaf-muon">AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It preserves zero support and caps row magnitude rather than forcing every nonzero row to equal length. Unit normalization can amplify small gradients and mishandle unsupported rows.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not enlarge a small gradient merely to give it the same norm as a large row.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01395">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01395-af-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-91844685fea05438">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:af-muon" data-paper-title="AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-62d1acd180b32cf2">How avoid NaN on zero-gradient vocab rows?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aaf-muon">AF-Muon: An AdamW-Free Muon Optimizer for Tied-Embedding Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 原文首页未列第一作者机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Branch explicitly: zero gradients get zero directions. Multiplying by zero after computing g/‖g‖ cannot clear NaN. Local checks verify support and cap, not paper-scale pretraining.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A row absent from both input and output gradients must not compute 0/0.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.01395">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.01395-af-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-62d1acd180b32cf2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bit-sparse" data-paper-title="BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-bit-sparse-b3242cb0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-91e3e0af62bbebf1">Why does BitSparse suit exact ReLU zeros?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abit-sparse">BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A bitmask stores positions, positive values are packed, and tile prefixes locate data. Reconstruction is lossless without approximating nonzero values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two positives among ten positions need two values and locations, not ten floats.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22256-bit-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-91e3e0af62bbebf1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bit-sparse" data-paper-title="BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8d6a729d709d628c">How can BitSparse save activations losslessly without recomputing forward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abit-sparse">BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>ReLU-family activations contain exact zeros. Store only nonzero values, a bit per position, and tile prefixes. Reconstruct for backward without quantizing values or rerunning forward. Savings depend on zeros and metadata.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For eight entries with six zeros, store eight bits and two original-precision values.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22256-bit-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8d6a729d709d628c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bit-sparse" data-paper-title="BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e0e29b6ea78fe4f7">How does lossless packing differ from checkpointing or quantization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abit-sparse">BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Checkpointing trades recomputation for memory; quantization trades precision. BitSparse exploits exact zeros. Sparse metadata and total training memory still matter.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With few zeros, metadata can offset packing gains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 结果与独立对照. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22256-bit-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e0e29b6ea78fe4f7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bit-sparse" data-paper-title="BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c1d398da0aac882a">Why not use one byte of bool per mask element?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abit-sparse">BitSparse: Compact Activation Storage for ReLU Feed-Forward Networks</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The format uses one bit per position plus tile prefix and positives. Byte masks change storage accounting. Check padding, zero sign, and backward formulas such as the 2H factor in ReLU².</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 32-position mask should occupy around four bytes, not 32.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与运行. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22256">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22256-bit-sparse/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c1d398da0aac882a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bmuon" data-paper-title="BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-bmuon-2e7cc5f8" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-18648aced26656c9">What prunable structure is BMuon designed to learn?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abmuon">BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It couples MLP hidden channel input rows and output columns under a common budget. This is optimizer geometry, not extra gates or arbitrary magnitude pruning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Consider both edges of a channel together.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23571-bmuon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-18648aced26656c9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bmuon" data-paper-title="BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-90c13d183e56fedd">Why share BMuon budget across MLPs and apply it to input rows and output columns?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abmuon">BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>One hidden channel is an input row and output column pair. A shared budget reallocates compressibility across layers and guides both sides&#x27; Muon geometry. It shapes training updates, not forward gates or post-hoc independent pruning.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 100-channel budget need not split 50/50, but paired edges use the same allocation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23571-bmuon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-90c13d183e56fedd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bmuon" data-paper-title="BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2a048970da0e26b7">How does global budgeting differ from equal per-layer retention?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abmuon">BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>All blocks compete for total K; fixed ratios preassign capacity per layer. Equal total channels can have different allocations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>One layer can keep more while another keeps less instead of pruning 50% everywhere.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23571-bmuon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2a048970da0e26b7">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:bmuon" data-paper-title="BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-711aa2a30cd60dce">Can BMuon reuse the old polar update after an MM budget update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Abmuon">BMuon: Budgeting Muon&#x27;s Spectral Geometry for Structured Compressibility</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Inria</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Use old allocation to compute MM scores, then recompute bilateral polar directions using the new shared allocation and one multiplier. Missing either paired gradient must fail rather than silently decouple.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A channel moving 0.2→0.8 needs directions based on new μ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 实现与运行. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.23571">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.23571-bmuon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-711aa2a30cd60dce">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-mixing-laws" data-paper-title="Data Mixing Laws: Optimizing Data Mixtures by Predicting Language Modeling Performance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-data-mixing-laws-e8c71fa2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-345a9b000888cf40">Why train small pilots across mixtures?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-mixing-laws">Data Mixing Laws: Optimizing Data Mixtures by Predicting Language Modeling Performance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge / Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Pilots observe each domain and support fitting mixture and scale effects. This reduces exhaustive runs but depends on coverage and modeling assumptions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Ten pilot mixes can shortlist others, not turn untrained points into measurements.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16952">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.16952-data-mixing-laws/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-345a9b000888cf40">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-mixing-laws" data-paper-title="Data Mixing Laws: Optimizing Data Mixtures by Predicting Language Modeling Performance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a72a4e046d49e6c">How do Data Mixing Laws search untrained mixtures, and what limits them?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-mixing-laws">Data Mixing Laws: Optimizing Data Mixtures by Predicting Language Modeling Performance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge / Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Small matched runs observe domain losses, a fitted relation predicts mixture/scale performance, and a weighted objective searches it. This avoids exhaustive large runs but depends on pilot coverage and assumptions. Keep final test isolated.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use pilots at 20%, 50%, and 80% code to select a few intermediate candidates; predictions are not measured large-model results.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16952">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.16952-data-mixing-laws/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a72a4e046d49e6c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-mixing-laws" data-paper-title="Data Mixing Laws: Optimizing Data Mixtures by Predicting Language Modeling Performance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-b7de02f902644429">How does fitted mixture search differ from measuring every mix?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-mixing-laws">Data Mixing Laws: Optimizing Data Mixtures by Predicting Language Modeling Performance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge / Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fitted predictions save compute but can have approximation and extrapolation error. Direct runs give measured outcomes at higher cost. Independently validate a predicted optimum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A predicted best 70/30 mix has not necessarily trained at target scale.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16952">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.16952-data-mixing-laws/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b7de02f902644429">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-mixing-laws" data-paper-title="Data Mixing Laws: Optimizing Data Mixtures by Predicting Language Modeling Performance" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-5c41aafffdf87cb9">How keep test outcomes out of mixture selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-mixing-laws">Data Mixing Laws: Optimizing Data Mixtures by Predicting Language Modeling Performance</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge / Shanghai AI Laboratory</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fit and choose domain weights/candidates under prespecified train/validation rules. Test once at the end. Mixtures are nonnegative and sum to one. A unigram proxy is not RedPajama scaling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not retune w_i after seeing test domain losses.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.16952">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2403.16952-data-mixing-laws/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5c41aafffdf87cb9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-orchestra" data-paper-title="DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-data-orchestra-f57d3169" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-26d35141723aa774">Why make chunk-level data decisions?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-orchestra">DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / SII-GAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Chunks differ in noise and quality. The orchestrator chooses Drop, Untouch, or Clean and organizes operations or instructions only when needed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Preserve a clean explanation while removing or repairing corrupted text.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24717-data-orchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-26d35141723aa774">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-orchestra" data-paper-title="DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-221959926fa7c86d">Why allow Drop and Untouch instead of applying all three stages to every chunk?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-orchestra">DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / SII-GAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Clean text can be damaged by costly rewrites. Choose Drop, Untouch, or Clean; only Clean plans noise pruning, surface correction, pedagogical augmentation, and per-chunk instructions. Plans are executed and verified. Optimize quality versus compute, not cleanup count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Leave a clean textbook alone, prune navigation on a web page, and drop a fragment missing content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24717-data-orchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-221959926fa7c86d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-orchestra" data-paper-title="DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-1ce48109d843ddae">Why preserve Untouch in sample-level orchestration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-orchestra">DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / SII-GAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It explicitly allows no processing, avoiding cleaning rate as a false quality goal. Per-sample plans select stages; one corpus pipeline can overrewrite and waste tools.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rewriting correct code may consume compute and damage content.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24717-data-orchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1ce48109d843ddae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-orchestra" data-paper-title="DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-aa1ba5f78ac0bb62">Can raw teacher plans be used as final SFT targets without verification?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-orchestra">DataOrchestra: Learning to Orchestrate Per-Example Curation of Pretraining Data</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Fudan University / Shanghai Jiao Tong University / SII-GAIR</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Execute tools and verify results; correct failed rewrites up to a limit and remove stages with lost content or insufficient change. Only verified evolved plans train the orchestrator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A format repair that deletes content must not remain a success example.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.24717">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.24717-data-orchestra/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-aa1ba5f78ac0bb62">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-quality-lsa" data-paper-title="Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-data-quality-lsa-d7c7a545" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-cde69f54fe549479">Why use linear regression to analyze pre- and post-training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-quality-lsa">Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Controlled linear attention exposes how covariance, initialization, and supervision affect weight prediction and permits closed-form references. It is not empirical evidence for full LLM training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Change task covariance in a small matrix and isolate how initialization affects fitting.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01293">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2603.01293-data-quality-lsa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cde69f54fe549479">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-quality-lsa" data-paper-title="Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a5caefc122995f3">Why isn&#x27;t OS in the data-quality theory full RL post-training?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-quality-lsa">Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>OS is outcome-supervised regression on final predictions. The comparison is SFT on teacher intermediate states. Linear attention and covariance assumptions enable closed-form analysis, not policy sampling, advantage estimation, or policy gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Squared error on final weights differs from intermediate-state matching without becoming reward-driven policy optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01293">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2603.01293-data-quality-lsa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a5caefc122995f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-quality-lsa" data-paper-title="Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-127313c1b546145c">How do SFT and OS differ in information supplied?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-quality-lsa">Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SFT supervises intermediate teacher weights. OS runs an autonomous rollout and supervises only its final prediction, without implying policy gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Stepwise standard results and a single final weight check are distinct signals.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01293">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2603.01293-data-quality-lsa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-127313c1b546145c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:data-quality-lsa" data-paper-title="Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-cb3026ef699d982f">Why must autonomous rollout not receive true w*?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adata-quality-lsa">Theoretical Perspectives on Data Quality and Synergistic Effects in Pre- and Post-Training Reasoning Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Ground-truth weights belong only in training loss, not prediction inputs. Use public context for rollout, feed targets only to the explicit loss, and preserve initialization&#x27;s nullspace in closed-form SFT.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A predictor cannot receive the exact weights it must recover.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.01293">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2603.01293-data-quality-lsa/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-cb3026ef699d982f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doremi" data-paper-title="DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-doremi-7bfdfa8e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6091e34a90a5668b">Why learn target-model mixtures with a small proxy?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoremi">DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Repeated large runs are costly. Small-proxy group DRO adjusts weights from excess loss, then target training uses that mixture. Transfer needs verification.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Estimate reference-relative gaps cheaply before allocating large-run data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10429">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2305.10429-doremi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6091e34a90a5668b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doremi" data-paper-title="DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-82c48593bd66c5dc">Why emphasize excess loss rather than maximum raw loss in DoReMi?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoremi">DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Raw loss mixes irreducible difficulty and underfitting. Subtract reference loss and use group DRO on a small proxy to derive target mixture. This is relative to the reference and data, not a preference for all high-entropy domains.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A has loss 5 vs reference 4.9; B has 3 vs 2. B&#x27;s larger excess can get more weight.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10429">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2305.10429-doremi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-82c48593bd66c5dc">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doremi" data-paper-title="DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-395b5c5a3e6e732d">How do dynamic DoReMi weights differ from uniform sampling?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoremi">DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Uniform probabilities stay fixed. DoReMi exponentiates reference-relative excess-loss updates and renormalizes, responding to underfitting rather than raw loss alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A high loss from an intrinsically hard domain may not imply a large excess.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10429">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2305.10429-doremi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-395b5c5a3e6e732d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:doremi" data-paper-title="DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-a08f39c27b1ec847">Why normalize α across domains after each update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Adoremi">DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Stanford University / Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exponential updates yield relative weights, not probabilities; normalization sums to one. Keep the same reference. Local two-domain unigram work is not a Pile 280M-to-8B transfer.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Relative weights 2 and 3 become 0.4 and 0.6.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10429">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2305.10429-doremi/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a08f39c27b1ec847">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:eco-optimizer" data-paper-title="ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-eco-optimizer-dd39c986" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-5b12a29e43a1976d">Why remove both master weights and a dedicated error buffer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeco-optimizer">ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / ISTA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Both consume persistent memory. ECO injects error into existing momentum to accumulate small updates without storing them separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>An update too small for one quantization step can still affect later optimization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22101v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2601.22101-eco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-5b12a29e43a1976d">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:eco-optimizer" data-paper-title="ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-60e5874d502e6a0b">How does ECO preserve small updates without high-precision masters?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeco-optimizer">ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / ISTA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Update quantized weights and feed requantization error into existing momentum without a separate persistent buffer. Compensation depends on step size, elementwise for Adam. The buffer-free derivation is approximate, not exact high-precision equivalence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A sub-grid update can leave weights unchanged but influence momentum and later steps.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22101v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2601.22101-eco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-60e5874d502e6a0b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:eco-optimizer" data-paper-title="ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3275fe9870f05c43">Is buffer-free compensation exactly equivalent to storing full adjacent errors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeco-optimizer">ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / ISTA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It uses an approximation that neighboring errors are close, with separate convergence analysis. It is not exact under arbitrary quantization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Large differences between adjacent errors can invalidate the approximation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22101v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2601.22101-eco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3275fe9870f05c43">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:eco-optimizer" data-paper-title="ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-77c5b857c061e0e0">Why can&#x27;t ECO use the same scalar coefficient when moving from SGDM to Adam?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aeco-optimizer">ECO: Quantized Training without Full-Precision Master Weights</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research / ISTA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bias correction and second moments create elementwise effective η_t in Adam; use that for error injection. Record quantization format and scale granularity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two coordinates with different preconditioning cannot share a scalar compensation denominator.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.22101v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2601.22101-eco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-77c5b857c061e0e0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gaugequant" data-paper-title="GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-gaugequant-8dce1822" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-3208d7926b6e1850">Why can activation outliers hurt typical values during quantization?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agaugequant">GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Fixed bit width must cover the range; large channels enlarge spacing for ordinary values. GaugeQuant learns an orthogonal basis with an outlier objective. Floating-point equivalence need not preserve quantization error.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A few levels spanning 1, 2, and 1000 struggle to distinguish 1 from 2.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20757">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.20757-gaugequant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3208d7926b6e1850">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gaugequant" data-paper-title="GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-be6020bebde4aa23">How can GaugeQuant change coordinates without changing the floating-point function?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agaugequant">GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Valid symmetries apply an orthogonal basis on one side and its inverse on the other. Quantization depends on coordinate distributions, so equivalent bases can yield different outliers/errors. Learn quantization-friendly bases only at valid locations.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Spread an extreme channel across several axes while inverse transformation preserves the floating-point output.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20757">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.20757-gaugequant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-be6020bebde4aa23">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gaugequant" data-paper-title="GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-a0afffd4b54bbb5b">How does GaugeQuant&#x27;s optimization timing differ from offline calibration?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agaugequant">GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Train bases and outlier objectives with the LM. Offline methods commonly freeze the model and calibrate from samples later. Bit width alone hides training and data differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Both can be W4A4 while one learns a basis during training and the other calibrates afterward.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20757">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.20757-gaugequant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-a0afffd4b54bbb5b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gaugequant" data-paper-title="GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-3e9baa60fb6616ad">How distinguish functional equivalence, fake quantization, and actual int4 execution?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agaugequant">GaugeQuant: Online Learning of Quantization-Optimal Bases from LLM Symmetries</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Check orthogonality and equivalent transforms, then quantization and gradients. STE fake quant can use floating kernels. The local work has no int4 kernel, so no throughput or bandwidth conclusion.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sixteen levels do not imply bit packing or int4 instructions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.20757">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.20757-gaugequant/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3e9baa60fb6616ad">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gemini-for-google" data-paper-title="Customizing an LLM for Enterprise Software Engineering" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-gemini-for-google-0c2d88a0" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0ae31377ea1cdc2c">Why not continue training on all internal code unchanged?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agemini-for-google">Customizing an LLM for Enterprise Software Engineering</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Extract high-value history and interactions, deduplicate, filter, and control contamination before midtraining and internal-tool post-training. Data curation and evaluation are integral.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Generated duplicate files and valuable fixes should not receive equal treatment by default.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16517">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2605.16517-gemini-for-google/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0ae31377ea1cdc2c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gemini-for-google" data-paper-title="Customizing an LLM for Enterprise Software Engineering" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-88875c261b2a4f2b">Why include general replay in enterprise code adaptation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agemini-for-google">Customizing an LLM for Enterprise Software Engineering</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Internal examples teach private code, tools, and workflows but can displace general ability. Replay adds a retention constraint; deduplication, filtering, and contamination controls protect the comparison. Validate both sides.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Learning internal build commands need not preserve general reasoning if training drops all general examples.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16517">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2605.16517-gemini-for-google/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-88875c261b2a4f2b">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:gemini-for-google" data-paper-title="Customizing an LLM for Enterprise Software Engineering" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-dbddc43401d20e73">What extra constraints distinguish enterprise midtraining?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Agemini-for-google">Customizing an LLM for Enterprise Software Engineering</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It includes internal code, interaction, and tools while controlling duplicates and evaluation leakage and preserving general ability. General training loss does not replace internal workflow evaluation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Memorizing old fixes can lower loss without helping new internal problems.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16517">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2605.16517-gemini-for-google/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-dbddc43401d20e73">Question link</a></p>
</details>

<h2 id="qa-853280a6dfb4900a">Why is Meta/AMD hardware diversity a co-design report?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahardware-diversity">Architecting for Hardware Diversity: Meta&#x27;s End-to-End Co-Design for High-Performance AI Training on AMD GPUs</a></p>

<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>

<h2 id="qa-1a1c64a8f0514de8">Why doesn&#x27;t CUDA-to-HIP compatibility establish performance portability?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahardware-diversity">Architecting for Hardware Diversity: Meta&#x27;s End-to-End Co-Design for High-Performance AI Training on AMD GPUs</a></p>

<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Running code does not align compute units, memory hierarchy, tiles, and parallelism. The work co-designs model, memory, parallel strategy, and kernels and estimates tail stalls. Hardware constants and optima vary.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A tile filling one GPU&#x27;s compute units can be limited by shared memory or tail imbalance on another.</p>

<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahardware-diversity">Architecting for Hardware Diversity: Meta&#x27;s End-to-End Co-Design for High-Performance AI Training on AMD GPUs</a></p>

<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The analytical model estimates compute, hierarchical memory, pipelines, and idle tail work. End-to-end results include actual workload and system effects. Neither constants nor local optima transfer automatically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A faster GEMM tile may be offset by synchronization or other stages.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:hilp" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
