<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c953a19c1dd72bb5">Why predict both next and abstract latents?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahilp">Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Local rollout may accumulate error; coarse targets constrain longer-term structure while preserving immediate detail.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predict the next word state with an auxiliary constraint for the next passage.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:hilp" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-988153cb726324b4">Why add a coarse temporal target to stepwise latent prediction in HiLP?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahilp">Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Small one-step errors can compound and lose distant structure. A coarse abstract latent supervises longer spans alongside next-token and local latent objectives. This does not eliminate rollout errors or replace long-horizon tests.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Predict the next waypoint and the next stage to constrain gradual route drift.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05806">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2608.05806-hilp/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-988153cb726324b4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:hilp" data-paper-title="Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Language Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">

<h2 id="qa-6430efce8e8df83a">How does coarse latent loss differ from raising the next-step weight?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ahilp">Hierarchical Latent Prediction for Language Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Texas at Austin</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Reweighting supervises the same horizon. A coarse target introduces a different span and structure, not simply larger λ1.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Doubling next-second loss does not ask for a prediction of the next minute.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lazyflash" data-paper-title="LazyFlash: Forward-Dense, Backward-Sparse Attention for Accelerated Long-Context Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">

<span id="paper-foundation-models-lazyflash-43455fcb" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-1694bf608c608052">Why preserve dense forward but compress backward?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alazyflash">LazyFlash: Forward-Dense, Backward-Sparse Attention for Accelerated Long-Context Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Forward determines visible context. Uneven gradient contributions let training sample/reweight backward blocks without making inference forward sparse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Read the whole document, then sample only some backward blocks.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31911v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.31911-lazyflash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1694bf608c608052">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lazyflash" data-paper-title="LazyFlash: Forward-Dense, Backward-Sparse Attention for Accelerated Long-Context Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-73f4f2504e86cd44">Why does LazyFlash save backward work rather than visibility?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alazyflash">LazyFlash: Forward-Dense, Backward-Sparse Attention for Accelerated Long-Context Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Forward stays dense. Output-gradient block norms set backward retention probabilities, and inverse-probability weighting estimates dense gradients. A tiled backward kernel must skip actual work; masking afterward does not. A single random draw need not equal dense gradients.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A low-contribution query block can be skipped in backward even though forward reads all evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31911v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.31911-lazyflash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-73f4f2504e86cd44">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lazyflash" data-paper-title="LazyFlash: Forward-Dense, Backward-Sparse Attention for Accelerated Long-Context Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-67cc8c10b70561d5">Is importance backward equivalent to fixed top-k gradient truncation?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alazyflash">LazyFlash: Forward-Dense, Backward-Sparse Attention for Accelerated Long-Context Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Inverse-probability reweighting targets an unbiased dense-gradient estimate in expectation; fixed truncation generally does not. Individual draws still differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A block kept with probability 0.5 is upweighted when sampled, not permanently dropped.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31911v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.31911-lazyflash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-67cc8c10b70561d5">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lazyflash" data-paper-title="LazyFlash: Forward-Dense, Backward-Sparse Attention for Accelerated Long-Context Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-360bcff30d297860">Why isn&#x27;t masking gradients after dense backward a LazyFlash kernel?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alazyflash">LazyFlash: Forward-Dense, Backward-Sparse Attention for Accelerated Long-Context Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Microsoft</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compute and memory traffic have already occurred. Skip tiles inside FlashAttention backward. No local operator or GPU receipt is claimed.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Discarding half the results after computing all blocks saves no backward execution.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31911v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.31911-lazyflash/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-360bcff30d297860">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lct" data-paper-title="LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">

<h2 id="qa-8f32908d4070ebe7">Why store exponents separately from sign and mantissa?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alct">LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Exponents are often concentrated and compressible. Preserve sign/fraction verbatim, use a fixed bounded code, and handle runtime center shifts without losing bits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Shared exponent patterns can compress while fraction bits remain intact.</p>

<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lct" data-paper-title="LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">

<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-74b7ca86cd3c25c0">Why retain rare exponents and overflow rather than drop them in LCT?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alct">LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Bit-exact recovery requires escape codes with raw rare exponents and raw overflow after stream exhaustion. Sign/fraction remain separate and a fixed codebook avoids relearning. This is lossless compression, not quantization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rare exponent uses escape plus eight original bits; overflow stays raw rather than becoming zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22179">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22179-lct/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-74b7ca86cd3c25c0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lct" data-paper-title="LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-95b48be5b7b4f2f3">How does bounded exponent coding differ from zlib on a tensor?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alct">LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>LCT specifies a fixed table, length cap, escapes, stream budget, and raw overflow tail. General compression does not provide that layout. Count codebooks and metadata in total bytes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Smaller payload may still produce larger total output after metadata.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 结果与独立对照. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22179">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22179-lct/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-95b48be5b7b4f2f3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:lct" data-paper-title="LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-549e6e120af7ef04">Why compare raw bits in LCT round trips?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Alct">LCT: Losslessly Compressed Tensors with GPU friendly execution for Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Cambridge</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Preserve signed zeros, subnormals, infinities, and NaN payloads. Numeric equality can miss these. Test all exponents, centers, and overflow paths.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>+0 and −0 compare equal numerically but have different bits.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 数据协议与运行. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.22179">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.22179-lct/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-549e6e120af7ef04">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:me-pois" data-paper-title="Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-me-pois-4510ed6c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-199f83ffcd54bde6">Why combine trajectories, prototypes, and text?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ame-pois">Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Sparse locations lack visits. Short trajectories connect to long-term prototypes, high-frequency anchors transfer temporal patterns, and text supplies semantic alignment.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A rarely visited place can borrow time-of-day patterns from nearby busy places.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2601.21149-me-pois/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-199f83ffcd54bde6">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:me-pois" data-paper-title="Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f585319aed43d6d3">How does ME-POIs transfer time information to sparse places?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ame-pois">Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>High-frequency anchors contribute within each spatial scale using distance normalization; then average scales so more anchors do not dominate. Trajectories connect recent visits and long-term prototypes; text supplies distinct semantic supervision.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Normalize two local anchors and 20 broader anchors separately before averaging their predictions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2601.21149-me-pois/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f585319aed43d6d3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:me-pois" data-paper-title="Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6858af52ff4ef838">How does per-scale normalization differ from one softmax over anchors?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ame-pois">Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize each scale independently before averaging. A pooled denominator changes relative scale weights based on candidate mass or count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Near and far scales each contribute one prediction regardless of candidate count.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2601.21149-me-pois/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6858af52ff4ef838">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:me-pois" data-paper-title="Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-7e4f3a1b6f155b38">Should repeated visits duplicate a place prototype as a negative?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ame-pois">Mobility-Embedded POIs: Learning What A Place Is and How It Is Used from Human Movement</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Southern California</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Eq. 9 uses distinct minibatch place prototypes. Keep temporal KL in direction r||q and sum across places as specified.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Three visits to a POI still supply one prototype.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.21149">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2601.21149-me-pois/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7e4f3a1b6f155b38">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:modular-robust-generative" data-paper-title="A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-modular-robust-generative-72932b77" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-141a2b81d1912e50">Why optimize worst-domain performance instead of average alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amodular-robust-generative">A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A good mean can hide severe regressions. Adversarial domain weights adjust input-dependent gates while respecting global probability mass.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Two strong domains can conceal one failing domain in the average.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2602.17554-modular-robust-generative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-141a2b81d1912e50">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:modular-robust-generative" data-paper-title="A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-8f5d8c105b8e3a12">Why doesn&#x27;t per-input gate softmax necessarily normalize a generative mixture?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amodular-robust-generative">A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Input-dependent weights cannot leave the global sum like fixed mixture weights. Local unit sums do not guarantee global mass one. Enforce total mass and distinguish worst-domain KL and NLL; silent post-normalization changes the objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A gate can choose the highest-density expert separately at A and B, making their total mass exceed one.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2602.17554-modular-robust-generative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8f5d8c105b8e3a12">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:modular-robust-generative" data-paper-title="A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-3a09d4a5fe88ce0f">Are domain KL and NLL equivalent for gate and adversary updates?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amodular-robust-generative">A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Within one domain they differ by gate-independent entropy, so gate gradients agree. Across unequal entropies the adversary&#x27;s ordering can differ. Local practice uses NLL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Subtracting different domain entropies can change which domain is worst.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2602.17554-modular-robust-generative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-3a09d4a5fe88ce0f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:modular-robust-generative" data-paper-title="A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-844919d92c1ac5cd">Why can&#x27;t cached noncausal teacher targets enter the router input?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amodular-robust-generative">A Theoretical Framework for Modular Learning of Robust Generative Models</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Google Research</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use them only as training targets. Causal router logits depend on prefix alone; the API does not prove the caller&#x27;s network is causal.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Knowing the target&#x27;s expert probabilities during training does not let inference inspect the target token.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.17554">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2602.17554-modular-robust-generative/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-844919d92c1ac5cd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon" data-paper-title="Muon is Scalable for LLM Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-muon-e884dc79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8161dcd10e677583">Why is Muon a matrix geometry update?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon">Muon is Scalable for LLM Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI / UCLA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hidden weights form linear maps. Approximate polar decomposition acts on momentum jointly and uses shape scaling and decay.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A dominant correlated direction is handled differently from independent scalar learning rates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.16982-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8161dcd10e677583">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon" data-paper-title="Muon is Scalable for LLM Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-93b41ee941026af3">Why treat gradients as matrices rather than adjust coordinates like AdamW?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon">Muon is Scalable for LLM Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI / UCLA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Muon approximates the polar direction of momentum for hidden matrices, then applies shape scaling and decay. This uses spectral relationships, not just elementwise moments. Non-hidden parameters still use AdamW in the large recipe.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Nearly collinear columns can yield different directions under matrix polar transformation and coordinate scaling.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.16982-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-93b41ee941026af3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon" data-paper-title="Muon is Scalable for LLM Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-d6c646312821684c">How does local Muon differ from applying it to every parameter?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon">Muon is Scalable for LLM Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI / UCLA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hidden matrices use Muon; embeddings, norms, biases, heads, and other parameters use AdamW. The hybrid optimizer is part of the comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A one-dimensional norm parameter is not suitable for matrix Newton–Schulz.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.16982-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d6c646312821684c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon" data-paper-title="Muon is Scalable for LLM Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-8a7420cefbab4d10">Why divide Newton–Schulz input by its Frobenius norm?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon">Muon is Scalable for LLM Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Moonshot AI / UCLA</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Normalize iteration scale before the specified polynomial; handle zero or tiny norms and preserve shape scaling. Orthogonality alone does not establish optimization quality or runtime.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Scaling a gradient uniformly should not radically change the iteration&#x27;s numeric range.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16982">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2502.16982-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8a7420cefbab4d10">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon-paired-budget" data-paper-title="When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-muon-paired-budget-6bbbedd2" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-9a0c27dfaf4180bd">Why report data, elapsed time, and tuning costs separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon-paired-budget">When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列一作机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Per-step and per-second quality and the cost of finding parameters differ. Equal-data gains need not hold at equal time or search budget.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Lower loss for equal tokens can still lose after one hour if steps are slower.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21555">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21555-muon-paired-budget/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9a0c27dfaf4180bd">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon-paired-budget" data-paper-title="When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-01050f98565ed331">Why doesn&#x27;t lower Muon loss at equal steps prove superiority at equal compute or tuning cost?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon-paired-budget">When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列一作机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Step latency, throughput, and tuning can differ. Pair initialization, data order, and candidates; compare processed data, elapsed training time, and fixed tuning budget separately. Freeze selection before test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Twice-slower steps can win at 100 steps but lose at ten minutes; retuning for time confounds the comparison.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21555">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21555-muon-paired-budget/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-01050f98565ed331">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon-paired-budget" data-paper-title="When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-4682ad997eed076f">Why isn&#x27;t random-access regret on a fixed candidate pool prospective adaptive HPO?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon-paired-budget">When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列一作机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It studies random order within precomputed candidates. Adaptive HPO uses prior results to propose or choose new trials, with different information and time costs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Randomly inspect 23 existing settings versus inventing a 24th from feedback.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21555">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21555-muon-paired-budget/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-4682ad997eed076f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:muon-paired-budget" data-paper-title="When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d0920c3cb6a09d74">Why sample the same seed indices in paired bootstrap?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amuon-paired-budget">When Does Muon Actually Win? A Paired Data-, Time-, and Tuning-Budget Benchmark</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · 论文未列一作机构</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Paired trajectories share initialization and data order. Mismatching seeds loses correlation. Integrate AUC over common measurement support and freeze validation-selected settings for all budget axes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Sample seed 42 for both optimizers, not 42 for one and 44 for the other.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 结果与独立对照. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.21555">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.21555-muon-paired-budget/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d0920c3cb6a09d74">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:musec" data-paper-title="Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-musec-4d47b01b" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-8636213a2e2d2ea8">What instability does Musec target?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amusec">Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Smoothly clip excessive momentum singular directions so they do not dominate Muon-type updates. Controlling spectrum alone does not guarantee better loss.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Limit a few huge singular values without equally scaling normal ones.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11655">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11655-musec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-8636213a2e2d2ea8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:musec" data-paper-title="Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-42029f8a35e58893">How does Musec spectral clipping differ from shrinking all gradients?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amusec">Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Smoothly constrain large momentum singular values without uniformly shrinking every direction. This changes update geometry, not proof of stability or final quality.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Control one abnormally large direction without multiplying every normal direction by 0.1.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式或操作. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11655">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11655-musec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-42029f8a35e58893">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:musec" data-paper-title="Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2be148601aabca00">What differs between smooth spectral clipping and a hard threshold?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amusec">Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Hard decisions can jump at the boundary; smooth mapping responds continuously. Specify the exact rule and budget rather than just claiming stability.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Slightly crossing a threshold need not abruptly change update magnitude.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11655">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11655-musec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2be148601aabca00">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:musec" data-paper-title="Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0cabe7890ac42e48">Does local full-SVD soft clipping establish large-model throughput?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Amusec">Musec: MomentUm SpEctral Clipping for Stable Muon-type Training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · National University of Singapore</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. It validates decomposition, smooth mapping, and reconstruction, not large training or optimized kernels. Verify numerical correctness and runtime separately.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Small-matrix parity does not establish cost per step on a large model.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.11655">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.11655-musec/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0cabe7890ac42e48">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-1b-audit" data-paper-title="OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-open-1b-audit-631edf79" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-ba2f25947a914bb4">Why audit states inside the training loop?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-1b-audit">OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gensyn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The final checkpoint does not explain its trajectory. Fix data and execution order and record hashes to replay and compare a specific step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>If drift starts at step 100, inspect its inputs and state instead of only final accuracy.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17380-open-1b-audit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ba2f25947a914bb4">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-1b-audit" data-paper-title="OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-eeaeefec1cc1f4e2">Why is a seed insufficient for auditing stepwise replay?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-1b-audit">OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gensyn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Batch order, kernel reductions, and collectives affect floating-point trajectories. OPEN-1B records them and per-step state hashes to localize discrepancies. Hashes detect but do not explain differences or guarantee cross-hardware parity.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Different summation order can cause drift; hashes locate the first differing step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式与实现对应. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17380-open-1b-audit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eeaeefec1cc1f4e2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-1b-audit" data-paper-title="OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-592091d76caabfd0">How does fixing seeds differ from fixing reductions, batches, and communication?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-1b-audit">OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gensyn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Seeds control only part of randomness. Floating reductions, batch order, and collectives must be explicit for replay; equal seeds do not imply bitwise equivalence across hardware.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Changing addition order can introduce drift despite identical initialization.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17380-open-1b-audit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-592091d76caabfd0">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-1b-audit" data-paper-title="OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-d2ae1e15043babee">Does matching a canonical hash prove full 400B-token reproduction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-1b-audit">OPEN-1B: A Fully Auditable Training Run</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Gensyn</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Local work checks fixed-order reduction and hashing. Full audit requires actual batches, states, and replay; a hash neither executes training nor proves correctness.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Equal hashes on two small tensors do not replay the paper&#x27;s entire training.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.17380">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2609.17380-open-1b-audit/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-d2ae1e15043babee">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-language-model" data-paper-title="OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-open-language-model-02ba0f0c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7a483d7ce6d15066">Why keep components as ordinary PyTorch modules?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-language-model">OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Madras</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Tight coupling to training and distribution obscures structure and ablations. Plain modules and composable wiring improve transparency and portability across notebooks, CPUs, and GPUs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Replace one block without also replacing the training framework.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.16669-open-language-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7a483d7ce6d15066">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-language-model" data-paper-title="OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-ae8ca0c028b6ef9a">How do composable Block, Residual, and Repeat help isolate ablations?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-language-model">OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Madras</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Separate ordinary PyTorch modules from wiring such as repetition, residuals, and parallel branches. This reduces coupling to the trainer and distributed execution and aids matched comparisons. Composability is an engineering property, not quality evidence.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Change serial to parallel wiring without changing data and training loop.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.16669-open-language-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-ae8ca0c028b6ef9a">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-language-model" data-paper-title="OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-6e6cdf128f84a999">Do DSL equivalence tests establish a better architecture?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-language-model">OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Madras</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Equivalence checks preserve semantics under rewiring; architecture studies test quality after changes. Near-identical PPL supports equivalence, not improvement.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Rewriting x+f(x) as Residual(f) should give the same result.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.16669-open-language-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6e6cdf128f84a999">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:open-language-model" data-paper-title="OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d6ef84afdcc27b9">How avoid incorrect Residual or Parallel wiring?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Aopen-language-model">OpenLanguageModel: Readable and Composable Small-Language-Model Pretraining for Education and Research</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Indian Institute of Technology Madras</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Residual(f)(x)=x+f(x); Parallel(f,g)(x)=f(x)+g(x). Check dimensions and repetition parameter sharing. Parallel addition is not serial composition, and not all upstream presets are local.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>f(x)+g(x) generally differs from g(f(x)) at the same shape.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.16669">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.16669-open-language-model/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d6ef84afdcc27b9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppl-factory" data-paper-title="PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-ppl-factory-5bbf227d" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-6acc0ef8d7d4889c">Why tie example selection to task and budget?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appl-factory">PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No fixed easiest/hardest policy suits all budgets. Task-specific frozen-model NLL guides easy, middle, or mid-random selection.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A narrow band at tiny budget may hurt coverage; random sampling within the middle pool offers another trade-off.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.18199-ppl-factory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-6acc0ef8d7d4889c">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppl-factory" data-paper-title="PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-0f2dc94cbdd47750">Why does PPL-Factory vary the selection band by task and budget instead of always choosing hardest?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appl-factory">PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Difficulty and usefulness are not monotone. A frozen model scores under the task protocol, and easy, middle, or random middle sampling trade learning signal and coverage. Reasoning SFT ranks response loss only.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>With dozens of examples, hardest-only can lack useful signal; random midrange may retain coverage, while larger budgets differ.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.18199-ppl-factory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0f2dc94cbdd47750">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppl-factory" data-paper-title="PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-bf9edb35a0895570">Can response-only and prompt-plus-response NLL ranks differ?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appl-factory">PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Yes. Full sequence includes prompt length and predictability; response-only isolates reasoning/answer tokens. Packed-block LM scoring is another protocol.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A long easy prompt can hide a difficult answer in aggregate NLL.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.18199-ppl-factory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-bf9edb35a0895570">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:ppl-factory" data-paper-title="PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-fa724c161c1899c8">Why match frozen scorer and starting checkpoint across subsets?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Appl-factory">PPL-Factory: Task-Aware and Budget-Aware Data Selection from Language Modeling to Reasoning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · McGill University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Changing score model or initialization confounds selection. Match block count and tuning budget; preserve negative transfer of middle selection and do not retune on test.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Random, Easy, and Middle must start from the same checkpoint to attribute PPL differences.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.18199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2607.18199-ppl-factory/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-fa724c161c1899c8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rkl-policy-distillation" data-paper-title="Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-rkl-policy-distillation-fa9bc42e" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c4f08e6c96bf34d9">Why care which states the student visits?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arkl-policy-distillation">Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Accumulate teacher/student KL under candidate-specific visitation. Equal weighting of all historical states can misrepresent actual risk.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A branch nearly never visited by a candidate should not count equally merely because it occurs in old rollouts.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30844v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30844-rkl-policy-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c4f08e6c96bf34d9">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rkl-policy-distillation" data-paper-title="Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-c10cf8835375ff57">Why not fit token reverse KL on old rollout states alone?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arkl-policy-distillation">Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Risk is under the candidate&#x27;s visitation distribution. The method uses clipped prefix importance ratios and cumulative KL increments for bounded candidate comparison, then updates whole-policy weights. Exclude current action and weight both sides of the difference identically.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A failure branch often visited by the old policy can be rare for the candidate and should not dominate.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30844v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30844-rkl-policy-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c10cf8835375ff57">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rkl-policy-distillation" data-paper-title="Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-9d74e89df11f1c35">How does full-feedback teacher information differ from a sampled answer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arkl-policy-distillation">Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Complete action probabilities enable reverse KL and candidate comparisons at visited states. A single sample does not give them. Teacher support must include candidate-positive actions or KL can be infinite.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Seeing A sampled reveals neither B nor C probabilities.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30844v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30844-rkl-policy-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-9d74e89df11f1c35">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:rkl-policy-distillation" data-paper-title="Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
