<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-c4630ce509123309">Why exclude the current action and apply the same prefix ratio to both terms?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Arkl-policy-distillation">Reverse-KL Policy Distillation: Statistical Guarantees and Limits</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Virginia</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>r_h multiplies actions only at u&lt;h and weights the difference of candidate and rollout cumulative KL increments. Including the current action or weighting one side changes the bounded objective.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>At state three, the arrival ratio uses only actions one and two.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.30844v1">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.30844-rkl-policy-distillation/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c4630ce509123309">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smrc-pmrc" data-paper-title="Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-smrc-pmrc-96d2a34c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0d48cc4c8b783203">Why not keep only the low-rank projected gradient?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmrc-pmrc">Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / Alibaba Token Hub</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Dominant singular directions can contain noise and exclude useful descent. Low-dimensional momentum handles in-subspace gradients; current orthogonal residual restores outside directions without full residual momentum.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A smaller useful direction should not be permanently excluded by a large principal direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19844">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.19844-smrc-pmrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0d48cc4c8b783203">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smrc-pmrc" data-paper-title="Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-00d2545fa87f1553">How do SMRC and PMRC recover gradient directions outside low-rank momentum?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmrc-pmrc">Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / Alibaba Token Hub</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use low-dimensional momentum inside the subspace and current raw orthogonal residual outside, without persistent full residual state. SMRC uses low-dimensional EMA; PMRC modifies matrix direction treatment, and basis changes differ. Neither is just projected SGD.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Keep momentum for two dominant directions while adding useful current gradient from a third.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19844">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.19844-smrc-pmrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-00d2545fa87f1553">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smrc-pmrc" data-paper-title="Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-52517eeea8c6108e">Why aren&#x27;t SMRC and PMRC the same optimizer?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmrc-pmrc">Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / Alibaba Token Hub</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>SMRC maps EMA momentum back directly; PMRC first applies matrix sign. SMRC corrects parameters at stage boundaries, unlike the theoretical PMRC shift rule. One projected SGD function cannot substitute.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Applying msign to M before mapping generally changes direction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19844">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.19844-smrc-pmrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-52517eeea8c6108e">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:smrc-pmrc" data-paper-title="Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-078fd6cd71d93be1">Why correct SMRC parameters and rerun backward before refreshing the basis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Asmrc-pmrc">Memory-Efficient Subspace Optimization with Residual Correction: From Momentum SGD to Muon</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanjing University / Alibaba Token Hub</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>At stage end, correct parameters and zero momentum. A new forward/backward at the changed parameters supplies the refresh gradient. A stale gradient mismatches state; local β weights the new gradient, unlike some APIs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Do not reuse the gradient from before the parameter correction.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 已实现的组件. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.19844">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../reproductions/2610.19844-smrc-pmrc/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-078fd6cd71d93be1">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:t-muon" data-paper-title="T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-t-muon-99464230" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-7bd4af109e8d4f82">Why put related matrices on the third tensor axis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3At-muon">T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>It lets layers, QKV, or heads interact through a third-axis transform before slice-wise polar and inverse mapping. Both grouping and transform define the method.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Stacking Q/K/V couples them instead of handling three unrelated matrices.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.24938-t-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-7bd4af109e8d4f82">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:t-muon" data-paper-title="T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-1d73398509874a34">Why stack related matrices into a tensor instead of flattening them for ordinary Muon?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3At-muon">T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Transform along the third axis, compute polar directions slice-wise, and invert the transform. This couples related matrices. Grouping and transform are separate choices. Restore original matrix scaling and zero rank-zero slices to avoid spurious updates.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Q/K/V transform-domain slices are not equivalent to one flattened matrix.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.24938-t-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1d73398509874a34">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:t-muon" data-paper-title="T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-75bd9f5e9dcf98a8">Why ablate grouping and transforms separately?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3At-muon">T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Grouping decides which matrices share a tensor; the transform decides how slices mix. Changing both confounds causes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>QKV with DCT versus heads with DFT does not isolate DFT.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.24938-t-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-75bd9f5e9dcf98a8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:t-muon" data-paper-title="T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-1f0938a0551233c2">Should fan scaling use head slices or original matrices?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3At-muon">T-MUON: Tensorizing Muon via t-SVD for Large Language Model Pre-training</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of California, Santa Barbara</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Use original fan_out/fan_in after reconstruction. Rank-zero slices must yield zero instead of arbitrary thin-SVD nullspace updates. Exact local SVD does not establish production polar throughput.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Even after slicing by head, scale using the unsplit dimensions.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.24938">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.24938-t-muon/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-1f0938a0551233c2">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taco-optimizer" data-paper-title="TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-taco-optimizer-aae79ac1" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-0322355f6e4728e8">Why keep one position per column?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataco-optimizer">TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Central Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>The max absolute entry yields a one-sparse signed direction and permits low-precision column-level state instead of dense per-parameter state.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A column with many nonzeros updates only its largest-magnitude entry this step.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02199-taco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-0322355f6e4728e8">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taco-optimizer" data-paper-title="TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-f73d70ba75b1e7db">How is one gradient position per TACO column different from elementwise sign?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataco-optimizer">TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Central Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Select the maximum absolute gradient row per column and retain only its sign. Low-precision column state saves memory. SignSGD updates all nonzero locations and is not one-sparse.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>[0.2,−0.9,0.4] yields only a negative update at row two rather than +,−,+.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02199-taco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-f73d70ba75b1e7db">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taco-optimizer" data-paper-title="TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-2cbbc3aaef1647ae">What differs between TACO and elementwise signSGD?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataco-optimizer">TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Central Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>TACO chooses one max-absolute row and keeps its sign; signSGD can update all nonzero entries. Their supports differ even though both use signs.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>For [1,−4,2], only TACO&#x27;s second entry is −1 and the others are zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02199-taco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-2cbbc3aaef1647ae">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:taco-optimizer" data-paper-title="TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-eec147661cf42971">What if TACO&#x27;s argmax runs along the wrong axis?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Ataco-optimizer">TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · University of Central Florida</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Maximize over rows separately for each column, not columns per row. Check zeroed positions and low-precision column momentum, not shape alone.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A 3×5 matrix has up to one selected entry in each of five columns.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 复现边界. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02199">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02199-taco-optimizer/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-eec147661cf42971">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tess" data-paper-title="TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="basics" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<span id="paper-foundation-models-tess-5d7b0b3c" class="ar-learning-paper-anchor"></span>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Basics</p>
<h2 id="qa-c02202de53c5a68f">Why make training-example value a learned prediction?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atess">TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Teacher loss gaps create pseudolabels, then a selector scores an independent pool. This amortizes expensive valuation rather than rerunning training across the large pool.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Estimate value on a small set, then score candidates unseen by the teacher models.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02092-tess/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-c02202de53c5a68f">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tess" data-paper-title="TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="mechanism" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Core mechanism</p>
<h2 id="qa-b2d1ae7150fa0a51">Why train TESS on loss-gap pseudolabels instead of directly optimizing selection?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atess">TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>Compare train-only and validation-guided models from the same initialization per example, then learn a transferable pointwise selector. Separating valuation from prediction avoids some degenerate direct objectives. Validation guidance is not test data.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Use loss changes to learn which examples help, then predict candidate value without reading test outcomes.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02092-tess/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-b2d1ae7150fa0a51">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tess" data-paper-title="TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="comparison" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Method comparison</p>
<h2 id="qa-e39e791601a4e3e3">How do loss gaps differ from selecting the highest raw loss?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atess">TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>A shared-init model pair estimates response to validation guidance; raw loss measures difficulty. Hard examples need not be useful.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>Persistent noise can have high loss without a valuable guided change.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 背景与主要改动, 核心公式. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02092-tess/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-e39e791601a4e3e3">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>
<article class="ar-learning-card ar-learning-qa" data-learning-card data-identity="foundation-models:tess" data-paper-title="TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)" data-learning-pending="false" data-level="implementation" data-domain="foundation-models" data-theme="foundation-models" data-topic="foundation-models/training-budget">
<p class="ar-learning-card__domain"><a href="./">Foundation models / Training budgets: data mixtures, objectives, and optimizers</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-level">Implementation details</p>
<h2 id="qa-190651bcfe1a3a18">Can selector gradients flow back through Δ_i into U/W?</h2>
<p class="ar-learning-paper"><a href="../../../all/?paper=foundation-models%3Atess">TESS: Scalable, Transferable Meta-network for Data Selection Requires a Different Loss (and Why the Obvious Choice is Problematic)</a></p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__meta">Question added: 2026-10-27 · Nanyang Technological University</p>
<details class="ar-learning-answer"><summary>Show answer and example</summary>
<p><strong>Answer: </strong>No. Train U/W in order from identical initialization and detach their saved loss gaps. Scores may be negative; do not use them as probabilities without transformation or substitute test for validation.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-example"><strong>Illustrative example: </strong>A negative value label should not be silently clamped to zero.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-sources">Sections in the Chinese source: 核心公式, 本地复现. The example illustrates the mechanism.</p>
<p class="ar-learning-card__links"><a href="https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02092">Original paper</a> · <a href="../../../../../foundation-models/2610.02092-tess/README-en/">Implementation write-up</a> · <a href="#qa-190651bcfe1a3a18">Question link</a></p>
</details>
</article>

<details class="ar-learning-guide" markdown="1"><summary>Topic guide and reading order</summary>

## Start with this question

Under a limited budget, should we change the data, the update direction, or the model size first?

## Takeaway

DoReMi learns a domain mixture with Group DRO using a small proxy model's per-domain excess loss over a reference, then transfers the mixture to target training. Muon approximately orthogonalizes momentum updates for hidden matrices with decay and shape scaling. Other parameter types cannot blindly use the same update. The first changes what the model sees; the second changes how updates move. Evaluate the axes separately.

## Example

A one-third split across code, web, and encyclopedia data is only a starting point. DoReMi uses difficulty relative to a reference, not the domains with the highest raw loss. After switching to Muon, compare matched-token, time, or FLOP curves, not one matched-step point.

## Common pitfall

A proxy's mixture is not guaranteed optimal at every scale; optimizer gains depend on learning rate and budget. Low-precision states, activation compression, and data selection can affect different resources. Retain the documented limits of mechanism checks, short-budget negative runs, and costly unreproduced experiments.

## Reading order

Start with why DoReMi uses excess rather than raw loss. Then study Muon's matrix update and limits for non-matrix parameters. Move on to data selection, low-precision states, and training systems.

1. [DoReMi: Optimizing Data Mixtures Speeds Up Language Model Pretraining](../../../../reproductions/2305.10429-doremi/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.10429)
2. [Muon is Scalable for LLM Training](../../../../reproductions/2502.16982-muon/README-en.md) · [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2502.16982)

## Check your understanding

Optimizer A lowers loss faster per step but takes twice as long per step as B. Does it use less compute?

??? note "Show suggested answer"

    Not necessarily. Decide whether the objective is time, FLOPs, or tokens to matched quality, then compare the relevant curves. Match training data and tuning budget. Per-step progress is not end-to-end efficiency.

</details>
